A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoLAR research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v5 reports original OOD detection results, semi-supervised classification accuracies, and component and hyperparameter ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports absolute OOD detection overheads in Table 3.

M1.justification: The exemplar mixture model, supervised and semi-supervised losses, SKMPS selection, vMF-SNE initialization, and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. The added projection-head explanation documents the existing architecture.

E1.justification: The OpenOOD ID/OOD pairs and classification and transfer datasets are unchanged. CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-200, Food-101, EuroSAT, DeepWeeds, Flowers-102, and Oxford Pets were already evaluated in v5.

E2.justification: v6 Table 4 adds FreeMatch to the reported CIFAR-100 comparison; v5 Table 3 reports it only for CIFAR-10. The other comparator memberships are retained. The corrected FreeMatch citation does not represent a different CIFAR-10 baseline.

E3.justification: The FreeMatch comparison adds a WRN-28-8/23M configuration for CIFAR-100 and changes the stated WRN-28-2 size from 1M to 1.5M parameters. MoLAR's splits, exemplar budgets, and training epochs remain unchanged. The expanded KNN description documents the existing evaluation setting.

E4.justification: The component ablations, training curves, exemplar-diversity analyses, initialization-transfer experiment, and hyperparameter sensitivity tests are retained. The new timing table expands reporting for the already-discussed full-data/exemplar comparison without adding an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run means and standard deviations for the specified classification experiments, the ImageNet-200 exception, 20-run exemplar-diversity reporting, and the distinction between repeated default settings and single-run alternatives in the initialization ablation.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports full-data/exemplar OOD overheads, including 0.15/0.0002 ms for CIFAR-10 and 0.75/0.002 ms for ImageNet-200. Table 4 adds FreeMatch's 62.0% CIFAR-100 accuracy. Existing benchmark and appendix scores match; the added overhead measurements do not establish a version-to-version speedup.

T1.justification: The model equations, assumptions, and appendix derivations are unchanged after renumbering. v6 Equation 10 explains the existing KNN metric rather than introducing a new theoretical contribution or changing the established method.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the specific 'up to 30 times faster' claim with reduced-overhead wording. The introduction also narrows 'similar to improved' exemplar-only performance to 'similar performance.' The central methodological and accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds specific limitations concerning backbone domain mismatch and expected failure where linear probing fails. It extends the existing appendix discussion of unsampled classes to class imbalance and many-class settings, suggesting classwise exemplar selection when labels are available.

D1.justification: v6 specifies the three-layer projection head with ReLU and batch normalization and adds hyperparameter-sharing and selection details. It also clarifies nearest-neighbor scoring and the two-hour, two-V100 training description, consistent with the retained Appendix D setup. These disclosures do not establish changed training.

R1.justification: v6 substantially expands positioning through a new prototypical-learning discussion, contrasting learned exemplars with fixed semantic prototypes and prototype-based logit smoothing. Section 2 also adds self-supervised OOD approaches, including CSI and MOODv2. These substantive additions go beyond the accompanying bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v6 adds explanatory subheadings, reorders related-work topics, moves existing representation and diversity discussion into Results, and separates the conclusion. Citation style and affiliations change, but most existing prose and the overall methodological narrative remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, extensively reflowing equations, figures, tables, and captions. v6 adds the timing table, adjusts table highlighting and its explanation, and relocates supplementary displays. The plotted scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: v6 makes the efficiency claim more assessable through absolute-overhead reporting, improves implementation documentation, and adds specific applicability limits and research context. These are useful refinements while the method and principal empirical evidence remain stable. The gains are limited: the timing table still lacks a detailed measurement protocol and does not demonstrate a new same-setting speedup.
